SMTO-GML-0015 — SMTO couldn't find that Gmail label

GUID: 5d1ffd66-11ff-49d4-abaa-846fca83bce2
Slug: gmail-label-not-found
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • SMTO tried to add or remove a Gmail label, but no label with that exact name exists in the Gmail account it is using. No emails were changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Gmail for the same account and check the label's exact spelling, including capital letters, spaces and any parent label. Use a label you created, not a built-in one like Inbox. SMTO only matches a label you made whose name is exactly the same.
  2. If the label doesn't exist yet, ask SMTO to create it first, or create it yourself in Gmail. SMTO won't invent a label while changing emails, so the label has to exist first.
  3. If you have more than one Gmail account connected, mention the right one with @ in your request. The label may exist in a different account than the one SMTO used.
  4. Ask SMTO for a new preview of the emails to change and approve it. The earlier preview was used up by the failed attempt, so a new one is needed.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the label change as done, and the emails show that label in Gmail.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to reuse an old label list if someone renamed or deleted labels since then.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gmail label-change preparation found no live label in the selected account whose exact name or ID matches the requested label (bulk actions also reject ambiguous matches and built-in system labels), or the provider returned 404 for the label.

What this means

  • Label-change preparation cannot match the supplied label name/ID in live account labels, or provider label lookup returns missing. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • Label-change preparation cannot match the supplied label name/ID in live account labels, or provider label lookup returns missing.

How to diagnose it

  • Refresh labels in the intended account and compare exact identity/name.

How to fix it

  • GmailService._label_changes matches label_name exactly (case-sensitive) against the account's current label names or IDs; workflows.label_changes (move_to_label, apply_labels, remove_labels) requires exactly one match of type user; a provider 404 on a label call maps to gmail_label_not_found. Verify the account_ref, list labels with gmail.labels, create the label with gmail.create_label if needed, then run a fresh preview (the earlier selection_token was consumed) before applying the change.
  • Refresh the live labels and select an existing label identifier.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The mutation names a current intended label in the correct mailbox.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
